title: Seek by desiring (Anselm, Proslogion 1)
hook: let me seek thee in longing, let me long for thee in seeking
tomorrow: what color is a soul that's coming back to life?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Bernard's riddle solved: the reason for loving God is God, and the measure is no measure at all. The line was without measure.

Scrolling listings for a house you can't afford. Rewatching the trailer for a trip you haven't booked. Wanting can be its own kind of looking. Anselm, a monk who became archbishop of Canterbury, opens a short book, the Proslogion, by turning that into prayer. But a few pages later, the same man builds an argument. So where does the search for God start: in the heart, or in the head?
screen: `WANTING AS LOOKING.` → `A PRAYER, THEN AN ARGUMENT.` → `HEART OR HEAD?`

segments.voice: First, the room. Anselm starts by talking to himself: put down the work, step away from the tugging thoughts, go into the inner room of your mind, shut out everything but God, and shut the door. Second, the honest problem. He admits he has never seen God's face and doesn't know where to look. He was made to see God, he says, and hasn't yet done what he was made for. Third, the line. He can't seek unless God teaches him, or find unless God shows himself. So he asks: let me seek thee in longing, let me long for thee in seeking; let me find thee in love, and love thee in finding. The chapter ends: he doesn't seek to understand so that he can believe; he believes so that he can understand. Fourth, the debate. In the very next chapter Anselm offers a famous argument for God. Later, Thomas Aquinas, also a saint, answered that this argument doesn't prove God to us, and reasoned instead from the world we can see. So, two real views. One: the search starts in longing and faith, and reasoning grows inside it. The other: reasoning from creation can walk a seeker toward the door before the longing comes. The Church honors both men.
screen: `THE INNER ROOM, DOOR SHUT.` · `NEVER SEEN GOD'S FACE.` · `SEEK IN LONGING, LONG IN SEEKING.` · `ANSELM AND AQUINAS.` · then, large: `SEEK AND LONG.`

segments.voice: Close your eyes and shut a door, a real one or one in your mind. Say Anselm's line slowly, half on each breath: let me seek thee in longing; let me long for thee in seeking. If the words aren't yours, stay with the longing itself, and let the wanting and the looking take turns.
Seek by desiring. Anselm's circle: the longing sends him searching, and the searching makes him long.
Your line: seek and long. In Anselm's prayer, each one keeps the other going. Goodnight for now.

howItsDone: Catholics honor both Anselm and Thomas Aquinas as saints and Doctors of the Church; Anselm's phrase 'faith seeking understanding' is often used to describe Catholic theology.

fork.setup: Mia says, "nobody can argue me into God." you're asked to give the best case for the Aquinas side. what is it?

fork.reveal: Aquinas reasoned from the world we can see, as a road toward God, not a trap. Anselm began in longing prayer. the Church honors both.

original.note: Latin for by desiring: Anselm asks to seek God by desiring, and to desire by seeking.

Abuela. Catholics don't use arguments for God at all; it's only about feelings.

chat.meaning: Anselm's book opens in longing prayer and then offers an argument; Aquinas reasoned from creation. Both are honored saints.

Anselm.meaning: a monk who became archbishop of Canterbury

Proslogion.meaning: Anselm's short book: a prayer that becomes an argument

Canterbury.meaning: an English city whose archbishop led the church in England

Thomas Aquinas.meaning: a theologian and saint who reasoned toward God from creation

sources.ref: Thomas Aquinas, Summa Theologiae I, q. 2, a. 1, reply to obj. 2; a. 3

notes: Proslogion 1 paraphrased. The spoken line 'let me seek thee in longing, let me long for thee in seeking; let me find thee in love, and love thee in finding' follows S. N. Deane's 1903 translation (Open Court), which isn't on the validator's public-domain list, so it is cited as a paraphrase with no quotation marks. Confirm wording, or mark it quoted if Deane is added to the list.

Confirm the chapter's order: the call to enter the inner chamber of the mind and shut the door; never having seen God's face; made to see God and not yet having done what he was made for; cannot seek unless taught nor find unless God reveals himself; the seek/long line; and the close, 'I believe in order to understand'.

Debate: Aquinas, ST I q. 2 a. 1 ad 2, answers the 'that than which nothing greater can be thought' argument (without naming Anselm) by saying it does not follow that what the name signifies exists in reality; a. 3 argues from effects in the world. The script says 'answered that this argument doesn't prove God to us, and reasoned instead from the world we can see'; confirm it is fair to both. No dates or time gap given.
howItsDone: 'faith seeking understanding' (fides quaerens intellectum) was the Proslogion's original title; the script only says the phrase is often used. Confirm both are Doctors of the Church.
